newsitem.title: UK: UK bank lending rises s/a 2,388 mln stg in January.
newsitem.headline: UK bank lending rises s/a 2,388 mln stg in January.

text.p: Total sterling lending by major British banking groups to the UK private sector rose by a seasonally-adjusted 2,388 million stg in January, the British Bankers' Association (BBA) said on Thursday.
"This compares with the exceptional fall of 536 million stg in December and an underlying six-monthly average increase of 2,186 million stg," it said in a statement.

Mortgage lending rose by 771 million stg last month -- the largest monthly rise since the housing market recovery began, the BBA said. In December, mortgage lending was up 643 million stg, while the six-monthly average rise is 619 million stg.
"Once again, it is the personal lending figures that catch the eye this month, particularly that for the major banks' mortgage business," Tim Sweeney, BBA's director general said.
He said January's 771 million rise was around 25 percent higher than the recent monthly average.
Consumer credit was fairly restrained in January, with a rise of 366 million stg lower than December's 414 million stg rise and the six-monthly average rise of 439 million stg.
Lending to the manufacturing sector overall was virtually flat, rising by just 31 million stg, the BBA said.

"Within this, there was a notable rise for the chemical industry (up 171 million stg), while food, drink and tobacco companies fell by 136 million stg, partly due to a repayment of December's short-term finance," it said.
On the liabilities side, deposits from the UK private sector showed a marked fall of 2,011 million stg, partly reflecting corporation tax and VAT payments.
